programme.desc: Wales is often called the land of castles, as it is home to some of Europe's finest surviving examples of medieval castles. It also has more ancient fortresses per square kilometre than anywhere else in Europe. Our journey will take us on an anti-clockwise route around the border of Wales and take in nineteen very different castles from across the centuries.

programme.title: The World From Above
programme.desc: We start our journey at the picturesque port of Oban, the gateway to the Islands. From Oban we travel down one of Scotland's most beautiful lochs to reach Glen Coe, with its impressive mountains and history of a chilling massacre. We fly over Rannoch Moor, one of Europe's last wilderness areas to reach the Cairngorms, and Scotland's only ski resorts. We then head West to Britain's highest mountain, Ben Nevis, before crossing the sea to the Isle of Skye.

programme.title: Ruby Wax: Castaway
programme.desc: Comedian and mental health campaigner, Ruby Wax, has tackled numerous daunting experiences during her career interrogating the Hollywood elite, but none more demanding than being cast away for ten days alone on a tropical island, 60 kilometres from mainland Madagascar. Inspired by best-pal Joanna Lumley, who was herself marooned for television 30 years ago, Ruby seeks hilarious advice from her on how to escape intact.

programme.title: Odysseus Returns
programme.desc: In Homer's Odyssey, King Odysseus wanders the earth for decades before returning to his beloved homeland of Ithaca. But archaeologists have searched Ithaca in vain for his city for almost 200 years. When Makis Metaxas, the mayor of a seaside village on Ithaca's neighbouring island, claims that clues in the Odyssey led him right to the door of a Mycenaean king's tomb, archaeologists were dumbfounded.

programme.title: Odysseus Returns
programme.desc: When Makis Metaxas and his wife begin to talk about the discovery of what they believe to be the tomb of King Odysseus, they expect they story will soon be known around the world. But the revelations of artifacts dating back to the time of the Trojan war only trigger a storm of controversy.

programme.title: The Secrets Of Mount Olympus
programme.desc: Once the residence of the gods in Greek mythology, Mount Olympus was celebrated by ancient peoples for its supernatural phenomena. Today, scientists are going to seek rational explanations of events which gave birth to myths, thanks to an exploration of the highest part of the mountain, towering 2917 meters above the Aegean Sea.

programme.title: Silent War: The Shadow Of Atomic Bombs
programme.desc: From Hiroshima to Kazakhstan, the film uncovers how nuclear powers turned remote lands and marginalised peoples into laboratories of the atomic age, hiding the deadly reality of fallout while perfecting ever-more powerful bombs and selling the arms race as protection and progress.

programme.title: Diana: The Princess And The Bodyguard
programme.desc: Ken Wharfe, Princess Diana's royal protection officer, shares the extraordinary story of their bond, part duty, part deep friendship. With unprecedented honesty, Ken recalls pivotal private moments he witnessed, and reflects on how the withdrawal of her protection may have shaped the tragic course of her final years. A revealing portrait of loyalty, love and loss.

programme.title: The Lost City Of Melbourne
programme.desc: In the 1850s, Melbourne was the fastest growing city in the world. They dreamt big, they built big. However, the attempted modernisation of the city in the 1950s destroyed much of it. Featuring rare archival film and photography, this film is a revelatory work that allows its audience to reimagine the former glory of the lost city of Melbourne.

programme.title: Genghis Khan's Mongolia
programme.desc: Using the latest research, we explore the rise of Genghis Khan, from outcast to ruler of the Mongol empire which, under his sons and grandsons, was one of the largest in history. We reveal they were more than bloodthirsty warlords, empowering women, embracing all faiths and connecting east to west and driving innovations from astronomy to the arts, leaving a lasting legacy.

We fly over Rannoch Moor, one of Europe's last wilderness areas to reach the Cairngorms, and Scotland's only ski resorts. We then head West to Britain's highest mountain, Ben Nevis, before crossing the sea to the Isle of Skye.

But archaeologists have searched Ithaca in vain for his city for almost 200 years. When Makis Metaxas, the mayor of a seaside village on Ithaca's neighbouring island, claims that clues in the Odyssey led him right to the door of a Mycenaean king's tomb, archaeologists were dumbfounded.

Today, scientists are going to seek rational explanations of events which gave birth to myths, thanks to an exploration of the highest part of the mountain, towering 2917 meters above the Aegean Sea.

A revealing portrait of loyalty, love and loss.

We reveal they were more than bloodthirsty warlords, empowering women, embracing all faiths and connecting east to west and driving innovations from astronomy to the arts, leaving a lasting legacy.

programme.title: The World From Above
programme.desc: Wales is often called the land of castles, as it is home to some of Europe's finest surviving examples of medieval castles. It also has more ancient fortresses per square kilometre than anywhere else in Europe. Our journey will take us on an anti-clockwise route around the border of Wales and take in nineteen very different castles from across the centuries.

programme.title: The World From Above
programme.desc: We start our journey at the picturesque port of Oban, the gateway to the Islands. From Oban we travel down one of Scotland's most beautiful lochs to reach Glen Coe, with its impressive mountains and history of a chilling massacre. We fly over Rannoch Moor, one of Europe's last wilderness areas to reach the Cairngorms, and Scotland's only ski resorts. We then head West to Britain's highest mountain, Ben Nevis, before crossing the sea to the Isle of Skye.

programme.title: Ruby Wax: Castaway
programme.desc: Comedian and mental health campaigner, Ruby Wax, has tackled numerous daunting experiences during her career interrogating the Hollywood elite, but none more demanding than being cast away for ten days alone on a tropical island, 60 kilometres from mainland Madagascar. Inspired by best-pal Joanna Lumley, who was herself marooned for television 30 years ago, Ruby seeks hilarious advice from her on how to escape intact.

programme.title: Odysseus Returns
programme.desc: In Homer's Odyssey, King Odysseus wanders the earth for decades before returning to his beloved homeland of Ithaca. But archaeologists have searched Ithaca in vain for his city for almost 200 years. When Makis Metaxas, the mayor of a seaside village on Ithaca's neighbouring island, claims that clues in the Odyssey led him right to the door of a Mycenaean king's tomb, archaeologists were dumbfounded.

programme.title: Odysseus Returns
programme.desc: When Makis Metaxas and his wife begin to talk about the discovery of what they believe to be the tomb of King Odysseus, they expect they story will soon be known around the world. But the revelations of artifacts dating back to the time of the Trojan war only trigger a storm of controversy.

programme.title: The Secrets Of Mount Olympus
programme.desc: Once the residence of the gods in Greek mythology, Mount Olympus was celebrated by ancient peoples for its supernatural phenomena. Today, scientists are going to seek rational explanations of events which gave birth to myths, thanks to an exploration of the highest part of the mountain, towering 2917 meters above the Aegean Sea.

programme.title: Silent War: The Shadow Of Atomic Bombs
programme.desc: From Hiroshima to Kazakhstan, the film uncovers how nuclear powers turned remote lands and marginalised peoples into laboratories of the atomic age, hiding the deadly reality of fallout while perfecting ever-more powerful bombs and selling the arms race as protection and progress.

programme.title: Diana: The Princess And The Bodyguard
programme.desc: Ken Wharfe, Princess Diana's royal protection officer, shares the extraordinary story of their bond, part duty, part deep friendship. With unprecedented honesty, Ken recalls pivotal private moments he witnessed, and reflects on how the withdrawal of her protection may have shaped the tragic course of her final years. A revealing portrait of loyalty, love and loss.

programme.title: The Lost City Of Melbourne
programme.desc: In the 1850s, Melbourne was the fastest growing city in the world. They dreamt big, they built big. However, the attempted modernisation of the city in the 1950s destroyed much of it. Featuring rare archival film and photography, this film is a revelatory work that allows its audience to reimagine the former glory of the lost city of Melbourne.

programme.title: Genghis Khan's Mongolia
programme.desc: Using the latest research, we explore the rise of Genghis Khan, from outcast to ruler of the Mongol empire which, under his sons and grandsons, was one of the largest in history. We reveal they were more than bloodthirsty warlords, empowering women, embracing all faiths and connecting east to west and driving innovations from astronomy to the arts, leaving a lasting legacy.

programme.desc: There's an emergency arrival at Battersea this week - a beautiful lurcher with a terrible injury in need of urgent surgery. Paul is on hand when he arrives to help calm him down and comfort him.

programme.title: Paul O'grady For The Love Of Dogs
programme.desc: Paul and the team are left baffled by a mystery illness which is making a young lurcher pup desperately ill. He also meets a gorgeous staffie who is too scared to leave her kennel.

programme.title: The World From Above
programme.desc: Wales is often called the land of castles, as it is home to some of Europe's finest surviving examples of medieval castles. It also has more ancient fortresses per square kilometre than anywhere else in Europe. Our journey will take us on an anti-clockwise route around the border of Wales and take in nineteen very different castles from across the centuries.

programme.title: The World From Above
programme.desc: We start our journey at the picturesque port of Oban, the gateway to the Islands. From Oban we travel down one of Scotland's most beautiful lochs to reach Glen Coe, with its impressive mountains and history of a chilling massacre. We fly over Rannoch Moor, one of Europe's last wilderness areas to reach the Cairngorms, and Scotland's only ski resorts. We then head West to Britain's highest mountain, Ben Nevis, before crossing the sea to the Isle of Skye.

programme.title: Ruby Wax: Castaway
programme.desc: Comedian and mental health campaigner, Ruby Wax, has tackled numerous daunting experiences during her career interrogating the Hollywood elite, but none more demanding than being cast away for ten days alone on a tropical island, 60 kilometres from mainland Madagascar. Inspired by best-pal Joanna Lumley, who was herself marooned for television 30 years ago, Ruby seeks hilarious advice from her on how to escape intact.

programme.title: Beautiful Game Changers
programme.desc: When Fangchen Liu could not find a football group for Chinese students in Sydney, he started one, creating a place for international students to connect, play and feel at home.

programme.title: Going Places With Ernie Dingo
programme.desc: Ernie's trip to tropical North Queensland finds him meeting a respected Kuku Yalanji Elder, a river guide who's made a sea change and an environmentalist who is determined to change attitudes.

programme.title: Odysseus Returns
programme.desc: In Homer's Odyssey, King Odysseus wanders the earth for decades before returning to his beloved homeland of Ithaca. But archaeologists have searched Ithaca in vain for his city for almost 200 years. When Makis Metaxas, the mayor of a seaside village on Ithaca's neighbouring island, claims that clues in the Odyssey led him right to the door of a Mycenaean king's tomb, archaeologists were dumbfounded.

programme.title: Odysseus Returns
programme.desc: When Makis Metaxas and his wife begin to talk about the discovery of what they believe to be the tomb of King Odysseus, they expect they story will soon be known around the world. But the revelations of artifacts dating back to the time of the Trojan war only trigger a storm of controversy.

programme.title: The Secrets Of Mount Olympus
programme.desc: Once the residence of the gods in Greek mythology, Mount Olympus was celebrated by ancient peoples for its supernatural phenomena. Today, scientists are going to seek rational explanations of events which gave birth to myths, thanks to an exploration of the highest part of the mountain, towering 2917 meters above the Aegean Sea.

programme.title: Silent War: The Shadow Of Atomic Bombs
programme.desc: From Hiroshima to Kazakhstan, the film uncovers how nuclear powers turned remote lands and marginalised peoples into laboratories of the atomic age, hiding the deadly reality of fallout while perfecting ever-more powerful bombs and selling the arms race as protection and progress.

programme.title: SBS World News
programme.desc: Latest reports and analysis of major national and international news of the day from Australia's only world news service.

programme.title: Diana: The Princess And The Bodyguard
programme.desc: Ken Wharfe, Princess Diana's royal protection officer, shares the extraordinary story of their bond, part duty, part deep friendship. With unprecedented honesty, Ken recalls pivotal private moments he witnessed, and reflects on how the withdrawal of her protection may have shaped the tragic course of her final years. A revealing portrait of loyalty, love and loss.

programme.title: The Lost City Of Melbourne
programme.desc: In the 1850s, Melbourne was the fastest growing city in the world. They dreamt big, they built big. However, the attempted modernisation of the city in the 1950s destroyed much of it. Featuring rare archival film and photography, this film is a revelatory work that allows its audience to reimagine the former glory of the lost city of Melbourne.

programme.title: Genghis Khan's Mongolia
programme.desc: Using the latest research, we explore the rise of Genghis Khan, from outcast to ruler of the Mongol empire which, under his sons and grandsons, was one of the largest in history. We reveal they were more than bloodthirsty warlords, empowering women, embracing all faiths and connecting east to west and driving innovations from astronomy to the arts, leaving a lasting legacy.

We fly over Rannoch Moor, one of Europe's last wilderness areas to reach the Cairngorms, and Scotland's only ski resorts. We then head West to Britain's highest mountain, Ben Nevis, before crossing the sea to the Isle of Skye.

But archaeologists have searched Ithaca in vain for his city for almost 200 years. When Makis Metaxas, the mayor of a seaside village on Ithaca's neighbouring island, claims that clues in the Odyssey led him right to the door of a Mycenaean king's tomb, archaeologists were dumbfounded.

programme.title: Odysseus Returns

programme.title: Silent War: The Shadow Of Atomic Bombs

programme.title: The Lost City Of Melbourne

programme.title: The World From Above

We fly over Rannoch Moor, one of Europe's last wilderness areas to reach the Cairngorms, and Scotland's only ski resorts. We then head West to Britain's highest mountain, Ben Nevis, before crossing the sea to the Isle of Skye.

But archaeologists have searched Ithaca in vain for his city for almost 200 years. When Makis Metaxas, the mayor of a seaside village on Ithaca's neighbouring island, claims that clues in the Odyssey led him right to the door of a Mycenaean king's tomb, archaeologists were dumbfounded.

programme.title: Odysseus Returns

But the revelations of artifacts dating back to the time of the Trojan war only trigger a storm of controversy.

programme.title: The Secrets Of Mount Olympus
programme.desc: Once the residence of the gods in Greek mythology, Mount Olympus was celebrated by ancient peoples for its supernatural phenomena. Today, scientists are going to seek rational explanations of events which gave birth to myths, thanks to an exploration of the highest part of the mountain, towering 2917 meters above the Aegean Sea.

programme.title: Silent War: The Shadow Of Atomic Bombs

With unprecedented honesty, Ken recalls pivotal private moments he witnessed, and reflects on how the withdrawal of her protection may have shaped the tragic course of her final years. A revealing portrait of loyalty, love and loss.

programme.title: The Lost City Of Melbourne
programme.desc: In the 1850s, Melbourne was the fastest growing city in the world. They dreamt big, they built big. However, the attempted modernisation of the city in the 1950s destroyed much of it. Featuring rare archival film and photography, this film is a revelatory work that allows its audience to reimagine the former glory of the lost city of Melbourne.

programme.title: Genghis Khan's Mongolia
programme.desc: Using the latest research, we explore the rise of Genghis Khan, from outcast to ruler of the Mongol empire which, under his sons and grandsons, was one of the largest in history. We reveal they were more than bloodthirsty warlords, empowering women, embracing all faiths and connecting east to west and driving innovations from astronomy to the arts, leaving a lasting legacy.

Today, scientists are going to seek rational explanations of events which gave birth to myths, thanks to an exploration of the highest part of the mountain, towering 2917 meters above the Aegean Sea.

A revealing portrait of loyalty, love and loss.

programme.title: The Lost City Of Melbourne
programme.desc: In the 1850s, Melbourne was the fastest growing city in the world. They dreamt big, they built big. However, the attempted modernisation of the city in the 1950s destroyed much of it. Featuring rare archival film and photography, this film is a revelatory work that allows its audience to reimagine the former glory of the lost city of Melbourne.

programme.title: Genghis Khan's Mongolia
programme.desc: Using the latest research, we explore the rise of Genghis Khan, from outcast to ruler of the Mongol empire which, under his sons and grandsons, was one of the largest in history.
